summary: Discovery call to qualify Silvershore's needs for reserved GPUs — they want predictable throughput for clinical inference windows with occasional spikes. Primary concerns: tenant isolation (VPC + on-prem path), burst prewarm model, eviction policies, and KMS/SSO compliance. Agreed to pilot and follow-ups.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-07 16:00 PST | Duration: ~47m | Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Maya Singh (Redwood SE), Dr. Elena Kovac (CTO, Silvershore), Marcus Reed (Lead ML Eng), Lisa Park (Security)

[00:00] Jordan: hi everyone thanks for joining, i'm jordan from redwood, i'll kick us off.
[00:08] Dr. Elena: hey, thanks jordan. quick note, we're in san fran so apologies on any background noise.
[00:15] Jordan: totally fine. maya's here from our solutions team, she'll handle perf / topology questions.
[00:20] Maya: hey all, hi.
[00:22] Marcus: hi. lisa's on for security.
[00:25] Lisa: morning.

[00:30] Jordan: objective: understand your production profile for clinical scoring, how big a reserved pool you need, how often you burst, and whether private deployment/VPC or on-prem's required. also timeline and stake holders. dr elena you wanna give quick context?
[00:45] Dr. Elena: yeah. so silvershore runs an inference service that powers triage suggestions for ambulatory clinics — it's latency-sensitive during office hours 8am-6pm, and we have big peaks after major data syncs and end-of-day reports. accuracy is critical — can't have model regressions — and PHI flows through some requests. hence the interest in dedicated or private.
[01:10] Marcus: to add, current stack is a mixed setup — we use hosted endpoints from a third party for experimentation, but we've seen variable tail latency during bursts and noisy neighbor behavior. Looking for predictable p95/p99 with reserve capacity.
[01:25] Lisa: and from security we need SOC 2, SSO/SAML, KMS integrations and audit trails. also data residency rules for EU patients.

[01:40] Jordan: great. quick qualifier: are you leaning more toward Redwood Dedicated (reserved pool in our infra) vs Private (VPC / on‑prem)?
[01:48] Dr. Elena: ideally dedicated to start — predictable capacity but still managed. private might be needed for some EU/regulatory customers later.
[01:55] Jordan: ok makes sense.

[02:00] Maya: can you give us rough QPS and token distribution or sequence lengths? it's ok to ballpark.
[02:08] Marcus: average concurrent requests during core hours: 120 QPS, typical sequences ~120 tokens, but some long form reports hit 1k tokens. burst windows spike to ~650 QPS for 3-7 minutes, maybe 2-3 times per day.
[02:28] Maya: helpful, and what's acceptable p95/p99?
[02:31] Marcus: business wants p95 < 180ms for the short calls, and p99 we need < 500ms if possible. for long reports we accept higher.

[02:45] Jordan: noted. how tolerant on eviction? e.g., if we need to preempt in infra events, do you want automatic fallback to hosted variants?
[02:55] Dr. Elena: we need failover with no dropped requests. ideally seamless fallback to a slightly cheaper model with degraded but safe behavior. can't have PHI leak to a multi-tenant host without encryption and logging.
[03:15] Lisa: to be clear: any fallback must preserve encryption-in-transit, we require customer-managed key or KMS logs.

[03:25] Maya: that's doable — Redwood Dedicated supports KMS + customer-managed key options and we can enable audit logs. for eviction, our warm-pool + prewarm strategies reduce cold starts. question: during your short bursts do you want guaranteed reserved GPUs for the full window or fractional warm pools with autoscaling?
[03:47] Marcus: we prefer guaranteed for the peak minutes. those spikes directly impact patient wait times. but don't want to pay for idle capacity all night.
[03:55] Jordan: that's where warm-pool and burst credit come in — you can reserve baseline capacity and then use burst to add prewarmed nodes for short spikes. billing can be structured (reserve + burst by minute). we'll send a few scenarios.

[04:10] Dr. Elena: curious about the "probabilistic burst" language you used in the invite — we run stochastic loads depending on synchronization jobs. how do you model that?
[04:20] Maya: we run burst sims using your historical load, and we model the tail with probabilistic windows — basically we size prewarm to handle X% of expected spikes, and fall back gracefully. there is some heuristics: warm-pool stickiness, eviction tolerances, and prefilling KV cache for common prefixes.
[04:40] Marcus: KV cache? we've heard of that but sometimes transcripts show it as K-V cash, haha. we rely on prefix caching for repeat prompts.
[04:48] Maya: yeah, KV cache — keeping key-value attended state on the GPU to skip recomputation, it's big for latency. we also can replicate warm cache to the hot nodes during planned increases.

[04:58] Jordan: on hardware, are you prescriptive? A100 / H100?
[05:02] Marcus: we currently have A100 workloads internally; our perf tests are tuned for A100. H100 would be fine but we need consistent perf numbers.

[05:10] Maya: good, we can pilot on A100 reserved nodes. our runtime metrics will give per-token latencies and throughput.

[05:18] [05:18] Dr. Elena: on isolation: for EU patient data we need VPC peering and customer-managed network egress controls. is VPC available with Dedicated?
[05:27] Jordan: yes — Dedicated offers private networking and VPC peering; for full on-prem we can discuss an appliance route but that's more involved. most customers do Dedicated in a VPC with strict egress.

[05:40] Lisa: also SSO/SAML for admin console and RBAC — we need audit trail retention for six months. do you support that?
[05:48] Maya: yes, RBAC and SSO integrations supported; audit retention is configurable as an enterprise add-on. we'll include the retention pricing.

[06:00] Marcus: two technical asks: 1) can we run a controlled preemption test (simulate eviction) and see failover behavior? 2) do you provide latency breakdown per token plus kernel-level profiling?
[06:12] Maya: yes to both. we can run chaos preemption in the pilot and share traces. our console shows per-token timing and a breakdown of kernel time vs queue time. sometimes transcription will call it "kernal" but it's kernel.

[06:28] Jordan: one common pricing question: how is burst billed — per-minute of added node + data egress?
[06:34] Jordan: (continues) we typically bill reserved monthly commit for baseline + per-minute for burst nodes and per-token for hosted fallback. will send examples.

[06:42] Dr. Elena: what's the minimum reserve you'd recommend for our profile?
[06:46] Maya: rough calc: baseline 120 QPS at 120 tokens -> that's roughly 2 A100 GPUs for steady state (with concurrency tuning). the burst to 650 QPS implies adding ~4–6 prewarmed nodes depending on batching. so reserve a small baseline (2 nodes) and pilot with 2 additional reserved that can be prefetched as burst nodes.

[07:08] Marcus: i want to see the math and sim.
[07:10] Maya: absolutely — we'll include the math sheet and a stochastic sim.

[07:16] Lisa: about keys — you said KMS. we use a cloud KMS in EU region, we need region-local keys.
[07:23] Jordan: Redwood supports KMS integrations and customer-managed keys; we can provision region-local key support for EU nodes in Private/Dedicated.

[07:32] Dr. Elena: on regulatory: for some EU hospitals we might need on‑prem eventually. what's the typical timeline to move from Dedicated to Private/on‑prem?
[07:41] Jordan: pilot to Dedicated usually 2–4 weeks, migrating to Private or on‑prem can take months depending on network and certs; we can provide a checklist.

[07:50] Marcus: curious on model rollouts — can we pin model versions and do canary?
[07:54] Maya: yes — pinning, staged rollouts, and auto-fallback to previous model on regressions. our Optimize toolkit can also recommend quantization profiles without degrading accuracy.

[08:06] Dr. Elena: data residency again — if a request originates EU but model hosted in US, does it count as crossing?
[08:12] Lisa: we need to avoid cross-border PHI.
[08:15] Jordan: you'd want regional deployment for EU-only PHI workloads — Dedicated in EU region or private in your EU cloud. we'll mark that as requirement.

[08:25] [08:25] Marcus: any constraints on preferred container or runtime? we use a sagemaker-ish pipeline for model builds.
[08:31] Maya: Redwood runtime abstracts the container; we accept standard model artifacts (hf, ggml or torchscript variants). packaging step is straightforward — we'll share onboarding docs.

[08:40] Dr. Elena: can we see a sample SLA for latency and uptime?
[08:43] Jordan: yes, Dedicated has SLA tiers. standard offers uptime + latency SLOs, enterprise adds stricter SLOs. we'll attach the SLA and highlight p95 targets.

[08:55] Marcus: about observability, we need traces per request and cost attribution by token.
[09:00] Maya: console gives token-level cost breakdown and per-route dashboards. we also support tracing integrations for your existing APM.

[09:08] Lisa: security Q: do you store plaintext prompts in logs?
[09:11] Maya: by default we redact prompts in logs for PHI; you can opt-in for full logs with customer consent and strict retention.

[09:20] Jordan: wrapping up the technical section — sounds like pilot: reserve 2 A100 nodes baseline, provision 2 additional nodes for burst simulation, KMS in EU for regional patients, run chaos preemption, and share perf sim. any other asks?
[09:33] Dr. Elena: include the regression-eval plan — we need to run our eval set to ensure quantized models don't regress.
[09:39] Maya: yes, include rollouts + evals in the pilot scope.

[09:44] Marcus: timeline? we want this before holidays — can we start week of 12/14?
[09:48] Jordan: yes — we can kick pilot provisioning 12/14 if contract OK. Jordan: i'll send pricing and pilot statement of work.

[09:56] Lisa: one more compliance note — we need vendor sub‑processor list and if Redwood uses subcontractors inside EU.
[10:03] Jordan: will include vendor list and subprocessors, plus SOC 2 artifacts.

[10:10] Dr. Elena: perfect. any closing clarifications?
[10:15] Maya: just to reiterate the preemption test and kernel-level traces — we'll run both.
[10:20] Marcus: excellent.

[10:22] Jordan: thanks everyone, i'll recap and follow up via email with the docs and SOW.
[10:27] Dr. Elena: thanks, talk soon.

Meeting end / notes: quick imperfect transcript, some speaker overlaps, occasional ASR errors (e.g., "K-V cash" for KV cache, "kernal"). Agreed pilot and next steps recorded in action items.

Recap (auto): pilot: 2 baseline A100 + 2 burst nodes; run perf sim week of 2026-12-14; Redwood to send SOC2, pricing, SOW, vendor list and onboarding docs.

Questions raised: what is exact burst billing, how to guarantee no PHI egress during fallback, timeline to move to Private/on‑prem.

End of transcript.
